drills.name: the shadow
drills.summary: bass only moves against the lead: lead up, bass down or holds — never the same direction on the same step

drills.name: pass the torch
drills.summary: the call in one voice, the answer in the other — one conversation across two registers

drills.name: oil and water
drills.summary: no perfect unisons or octaves between the voices on any coincident step

drills.name: the latecomer ✗
drills.summary: failed by design 2026-07-31 — the suspension returns with holds (L3.2)
drills.teaches: a drill that punishes the ear for liking things is badly built

drills.name: the drone
drills.summary: the bass holds one pitch the entire loop; the melody alone makes motion, tension, release

drills.name: contour drone
drills.summary: the closed drone: mediant drone with a density contour
drills.teaches: how much harmony one stubborn note implies

drills.name: relentless drone
drills.summary: the relentless variant — filed as a section motif for when form exists

drills.name: hocket: the hiccup
drills.summary: never share a step / at most two rests / no voice twice in a row / one octave

drills.name: hocket: the handoff
drills.summary: never share a step / at most four rests, none adjacent / handoffs every 2-3 notes, never one, never four
drills.teaches: the groove lives in the handoff

drills.name: hocket: the snap
drills.summary: never share a step / at most two rests / lead an octave above bass, always

drills.name: ostinato
drills.summary: the bass is an unbroken four-note cell; the melody must not phrase in fours

drills.name: Ostinato Variant
drills.summary: the F-F-E cell with one substitution at the seam
drills.teaches: one rule-break, placed where it lands

drills.name: L2 Candidate I
drills.summary: the L2 deliverable: C-major contrappunto wedge, bare-tritone implied G7, stray D#
drills.teaches: the letter of the law, served

drills.name: L2 Candidate II
drills.summary: the ostinato cell that climbs out of its own floor; keystone runner-up

drills.name: the long note
drills.summary:
- exactly one note of four steps or more
- every other note two steps or fewer

drills.name: all ring
drills.summary:
- no silent steps anywhere
- at least three different note lengths

drills.name: ring the seam
drills.summary:
- one note rings across the loop seam
- step 1 strikes nothing
drills.teaches: the seam is a place, not a wall.

drills.name: two breaths
drills.summary:
- exactly two silent steps, not adjacent
- exactly two notes of three steps or more
drills.teaches: a rest and a hold are different breaths.

drills.name: the apprentice's hand
drills.summary:
- transcribe 16 steps of a Uematsu line, recording playing
- change exactly four steps until it is yours
- keep both; play them back to back
drills.teaches: the distance between imitation and voice is about four decisions.

drills.name: steal the beat
drills.summary:
- no strike on steps 5, 9, 13
- a held note sounds on each

drills.name: threes
drills.summary:
- every note exactly three steps long
- at least five notes

drills.name: daylight
drills.summary:
- steps 1–8: every note rings into the next
- steps 9–16: every note cut short before the next

drills.name: give way
drills.summary:
- exactly two lead notes of three steps or more
- each one's next note: one step down
- the bass strikes under each

drills.name: the drone II
drills.summary:
- the bass strikes exactly once
- that note rings all sixteen steps
- the lead rests at least twice

drills.name: the ceiling
drills.summary:
- the highest lead note rings six steps or more
- the bass strikes four times beneath it

drills.name: dovetail
drills.summary:
- the voices never rest on the same step
- each voice rests at least twice

drills.name: ring the seam II
drills.summary:
- one voice rings across the seam
- the other strikes on step 1

drills.name: the glacier
drills.summary:
- every lead note three steps or more
- every bass note exactly one step

drills.name: the elder's line
drills.summary:
- every lead note rings two steps or more
- the lead never strikes where the bass does

drills.name: hand-me-down
drills.summary:
- every sealed note is renamed
- no note repeats its neighbour
- the bass strikes at least three times
drills.teaches: melody and rhythm are separate clays.

drills.name: the keystone
drills.summary:
- no lead note above the sealed one
- no lead note rings longer
- the bass strikes twice while it rings

drills.name: the stray, planted
drills.summary:
- its next lead note: one step down
- a bass note rings beneath it

drills.name: the tide
drills.summary:
- the bass strikes exactly twice
- no silent bass step anywhere
- the two bass notes differ
- the lead rests at least four times

drills.name: twice told
drills.summary:
- the bass strikes exactly once
- that note rings all thirty-two
- lead 17–32 repeats lead 1–16
- exactly four steps differ

drills.name: the elder slows
drills.summary:
- every lead note rings two steps or more
- the lead never strikes where the bass does
drills.teaches: writing against a line that slows.

drills.name: the elder's heir
drills.summary:
- bass 17–32: exactly four notes
- each bass note rings four steps
- every lead note rings two steps or more
- the lead never strikes where the bass does
drills.teaches: finishing a line you didn't start.

drills.name: the gates
drills.summary:
- no other lead note wears their name
- no bass note wears it either
- the bass strikes at least four times

drills.name: ballast
drills.summary:
- every unsealed lead note: one step
- the bass strikes under each sealed note
- the bass strikes nowhere else

drills.name: the return
drills.summary:
- lead 25–32 repeats lead 1–8
- bass 25–32 repeats bass 1–8
- steps 9–24: at least six lead notes

drills.name: prose
drills.summary:
- a rest ends every lead phrase
- at least four lead phrases
- no two phrases the same length
- every bass note rings four or more

drills.name: before the bell
drills.summary:
- no silent bass step anywhere
- every bass note rings four steps
- steps 1–8: at least four lead notes
- steps 9–14: at least two lead notes

drills.name: four rooms
drills.summary:
- the sealed note rings four different lengths
- every unsealed bass note: one step
- every lead note rings two steps or more
drills.teaches: the ring belongs to the room.
